title: Refusal Direction Transfer Across Chat Templates and System Prompts

original_idea.body:
# Refusal Direction Transfer Across Chat Templates and System Prompts

**Problem:** It is unverified whether a refusal direction extracted under one template still mediates refusal under a different template/system prompt.

**Direction:** Extract the difference-of-means refusal direction under default template. Evaluate steering under (a) no system prompt, (b) maximally-helpful system prompt, (c) an alternate chat template. Report direction-transfer robustness.

**Why it matters:** If a refusal direction is template-fragile, jailbreaks via template manipulation become a predictable attack surface.

**Relevant context:** Arditi et al. (NeurIPS 2024); steering vectors are sensitive to prompt distribution.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: template-fragile refusal directions imply a predictable jailbreak attack surface, deployment-relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Standard difference-of-means + template variation; guided, novice+mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single-model experiment across a few template/system-prompt conditions.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-weight deployment-config study labs deprioritize; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Single open chat model inference, one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Steering-vector prompt sensitivity is noted; isolating template/system-prompt transfer for refusal may be open.
